study_design: Biopsy-based case-control/cross-sectional analysis of subjects undergoing prostate biopsy because of elevated PSA.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: This study explored associations and interactions between genetic and environmental risk factors on the risk of prostate cancer (PCa) in 323 subjects that underwent prostate biopsy due to prostate specific antigen (PSA) levels above 4 ng/ml (161 PCa and 162 non-PCa).
reason: The abstract associates soy intake with overall prostate cancer risk. Although some genetic polymorphisms were associated with Gleason score, it does not establish an aggressive incident prostate cancer analysis for soy.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The intake of nuts and soya products was associated with a reduced risk of PCa, as well as the performance of physical activity.
estimate_classifications.reason: The soy association is explicitly with overall prostate cancer, without an aggressive endpoint or a numeric effect and 95% confidence interval.
